claim_text: The economy is rigged against working people
neutral_phrasing: The economic system contains structures and policies that disproportionately benefit some groups over others, affecting wealth distribution and opportunities for workers.

nodes.title: Structural inequality - Wikipedia
nodes.exact_phrasing: the fabric of organizations, institutions, governments or social networks contains an embedded cultural, linguistic, economic, religious/belief, physical or identity based bias which provides advantages for some members and marginalizes or produces disadvantages for other members. This can involve...unequal access to health care, housing, education...financial resources or other social opportunities.

nodes.title: Structural Inequality: Origins and Quests for Solutions in Old Worlds and New | Springer Nature Link
nodes.author: Roger D. Norton
nodes.exact_phrasing: bedrock types of inequality whose origins are rooted in the history and culture of each country. These kinds of inequality strongly influence income distributions by strata, can be resistant to change, and require solutions beyond fiscal tax and expenditure policies

nodes.title: The Dynamics of Wealth Inequality and the Effect of Income Distribution | PLOS One
nodes.author: Yonatan Berman, Eshel Ben-Jacob, Yoash Shapira
nodes.exact_phrasing: The rapid increase of wealth inequality in the past few decades is one of the most disturbing social and economic issues of our time... Wealth inequality is generally thought to impose instabilities on economies and on the social structure of countries... controlling the distribution of income, using income tax or other macroeconomic policy instruments, is generally perceived as effective for regulating the wealth distribution.
nodes.attribution_text: generally perceived as effective; generally thought to impose instabilities

nodes.title: Joseph Stiglitz – inequality is not an inevitable consequence of capitalism - LSE Review of Books
nodes.author: Ivan Radanović
nodes.exact_phrasing: inequality is not inherent to capitalism, but the result of systemic policy failures, rent-seeking behaviour and abuse of market power
nodes.attribution_text: Joseph Stiglitz argues in his book 'The Origins of Inequality, and Policies to Contain It'

parents.evidence: Both sources emphasize rent-seeking behavior and institutional failures as drivers of inequality; the LSE review's framing of 'systemic policy failures, rent-seeking behaviour and abuse of market power' closely echoes the institutional/rent-seeking language in the 2020 Springer journal article, though the LSE piece explicitly attributes to Stiglitz rather than to the journal article itself.

The LSE review's discussion of inequality as a systemic outcome aligns thematically with the PLOS ONE framing of wealth inequality as a structural and policy problem, though no direct citation is made.

nodes.title: Comparative analysis of the effects of institutional factors and Piketty’s Hypothesis on inequality: evidence from a panel of countries | Journal of Economic Structures | Full Text
nodes.author: Ali Sarkhosh-Sara, Khadije Nasrollahi, Karim Azarbayjani, Rasul Bakhshi Dastjerdi
nodes.exact_phrasing: economic and political institutions are produced by the endogenous distribution of political power, causing different income distributions. This explains the failure of political and economic institutions to control rent-seeking behavior that results in growing inequality. As a result, inequality derived from the poor institutional quality can be mainly considered as the failure of institutions to operate appropriately.
nodes.attribution_text: Institutional approach; references to Acemoglu and Robinson 2015 for institutional structures; Marx and Ricardo for capitalistic system inequality
